label: final original token w (or <DEL>) at end of a length-9 sequence, sparse
explanation: A very sparse feature that fires only at the end of the original phase in long sequences. Nearly all activity is at t=8 or t=9 with L=9 (93% of mass; a little at L=8). There are two sites: (1) the 9th original token when it is w (50% of mass, and it carries the strongest activations, up to max) and (2) the <DEL> step (46% of mass, usually weaker, often right after a w activation). It never fires in the copy phase, never before t=7, and never on sequences with L<=7. Even inside this context it is very selective: only about 16% of L=9 sequences ending in w activate, and under 1% of L=9 <DEL> steps do. Which ones fire depends on the earlier sequence contents in a way no simple predicate captured. First token y/c/j and i at position 2 are enriched, and prev_tok q is enriched at <DEL>, but these raise precision only at a large cost in recall. The predicate covers the w site only (dev F1 0.22, mass recall 0.48). The broader context predicate (L=9, last token w, or <DEL>) reaches 0.88 mass recall at about 1% precision.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=y (+3.92), orig2=i (+3.90), orig3=i (+3.03), prev_tok=q (+2.90), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=w (+2.79), phase=0 & in_tok=w (+2.79). Lower it: next_out=- (-4.80), orig7=- (-3.94), in_count=1 (-3.26), phase=2 (-3.12).
